name: Two sketches of a stag, and (on the reverse) a harpsichord
summary: Two sketches (one very slight) of a stag lying on the ground. On the back a drawing of a harpsichord is identified in the shorthand inscription as being 'at Mrs Leighton's' - a reference probably to Sarah Layton (née Rea) who married Temple Hillyard Layton of the consular service in Macau in 1837.
